records.source: וַיְהִי֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁמִינִ֔י קָרָ֣א מֹשֶׁ֔ה לְאַהֲרֹ֖ן וּלְבָנָ֑יו וּלְזִקְנֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And it was on the day the eighth, summoned Moses Aaron and his sons and [the] elders of Israel.
pieces: When the eighth day came, Moses called for Aaron and his sons and for the elders of Israel.

L.1: And it came about on the eighth day [that] Moses summoned Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel.

R.1: On the eighth day Moses called Aaron and his sons together. He also called the leaders of Israel.

decisions.choice: the eighth day: the day after the seven days of ordination
decisions.reason: Aaron and his sons had stayed at the entrance of the tent for the seven days of their ordination (8:33-35). On the next day, the eighth, they begin to serve as priests. The eighth day also marks a new beginning elsewhere in the law: a newborn animal may be offered from its eighth day (22:27), and a person cleansed from skin disease or a discharge brings offerings on the eighth day (14:10, 23; 15:14, 29).

decisions.choice: the elders of Israel: the leaders who act for the people
decisions.reason: The elders were the heads of the tribes and families, who stood for the whole people (4:15; Exodus 3:16; 24:1, 9). They are called with the priests because the people's own offerings are to be brought this day (verse 3).

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: Readable says what the elders were. Literal and Balanced keep "elders".

records.heading: Aaron offers the first sacrifices

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֗ן קַח־לְ֠ךָ עֵ֣גֶל בֶּן־בָּקָ֧ר לְחַטָּ֛את וְאַ֥יִל לְעֹלָ֖ה תְּמִימִ֑ם וְהַקְרֵ֖ב לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he said to Aaron, take for yourself [a] calf, [a] son of [the] herd, for [a] sin offering, and [a] ram for [a] burnt offering, unblemished, and bring near before Yahweh.
pieces: He told Aaron, "Choose a young calf from the herd as a sin offering for yourself, and a ram as a burnt offering, each without defect, and bring them before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.2: And he said to Aaron, "Take for yourself a calf, a young one of the herd, for a sin offering, and a ram for a burnt offering, unblemished, and bring [them] near before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.2: He told Aaron, "Get a young calf for a sin offering for yourself. Also get a ram for a burnt offering. They must have nothing wrong with them. Bring them to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: a calf, a young one of the herd: a young male of the cattle
decisions.reason: The word is the one for a calf or young bull (Exodus 32:4; Micah 6:6). The law for the anointed priest's sin offering names a bull (4:3), and so did the ordination (8:14); on this first day Aaron brings a calf. The text does not say why. For the sin offering see 4:3, and for the burnt offering 1:3.

decisions.choice: take for yourself: Aaron's first offerings are for his own sin
decisions.reason: Before Aaron offers for the people (verses 3, 15), he offers for himself (verses 7-8). The priest who makes atonement for others needs atonement too (8:34; 16:6; Hebrews 5:3; 7:27).

decisions.choice: unblemished: whole, with no defect
decisions.reason: The plural covers both animals. See 1:3.

decisions.choice: each without defect (Balanced); They must have nothing wrong with them (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that the rule applies to both animals.

records.source: וְאֶל־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל תְּדַבֵּ֣ר לֵאמֹ֑ר קְח֤וּ שְׂעִיר־עִזִּים֙ לְחַטָּ֔את וְעֵ֨גֶל וָכֶ֧בֶשׂ בְּנֵי־שָׁנָ֛ה תְּמִימִ֖ם לְעֹלָֽה׃
records.gloss: And to [the] sons of Israel you will speak, saying, take [a] male goat of [the] goats for [a] sin offering, and [a] calf and [a] lamb, sons of [a] year, unblemished, for [a] burnt offering,
pieces: And say to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, 'Bring a male goat for a sin offering, and for a burnt offering a calf and a lamb, year-old animals without defect,

L.3: And to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel you will speak, saying, 'Take a male goat for a sin offering, and a calf and a lamb, a year old, unblemished, for a burnt offering,

R.3: Then tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, 'Bring a male goat for a sin offering. Also bring a calf and a lamb for a burnt offering. They must be one year old, with nothing wrong with them.

decisions.choice: you will speak: Moses tells Aaron to give the people their instructions
decisions.reason: The verb is addressed to Aaron, who now speaks to the people as their priest. In verse 5 the people bring "what Moses commanded", since the command came through Moses.

decisions.choice: a male goat for a sin offering: the people's offering for sin
decisions.reason: The sin offering of the whole congregation in 4:14 is a bull; here, as on the Day of Atonement (16:5, 15), the people's sin offering is a male goat. A male goat is also the sin offering of a leader (4:23). For the sin offering see 4:3.

decisions.choice: sons of a year: a year old
decisions.reason: "Son of a year" is the Hebrew way of giving an age: animals in their first year (12:6; 23:12; Exodus 12:5). The words apply to both the calf and the lamb.

records.source: וְשׁ֨וֹר וָאַ֜יִל לִשְׁלָמִ֗ים לִזְבֹּ֨חַ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וּמִנְחָ֖ה בְּלוּלָ֣ה בַשָּׁ֑מֶן כִּ֣י הַיּ֔וֹם יְהוָ֖ה נִרְאָ֥ה אֲלֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: and [an] ox and [a] ram for peace offerings, to sacrifice before Yahweh, and [a] grain offering mixed with oil; for today Yahweh appears to you.
pieces: and an ox and a ram to be sacrificed before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a peace offering, and a grain offering mixed with oil. For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will appear to you today.'"

L.4: and an ox and a ram for peace offerings, to sacrifice before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and a grain offering mixed with oil; for today {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will appear to you.'"

R.4: Bring an ox and a ram for a peace offering, to sacrifice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And bring a grain offering mixed with oil. Do this, because today {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will appear to you.'"

decisions.choice: an ox and a ram for peace offerings, and a grain offering: the whole set of offerings
decisions.reason: With the sin offering and the burnt offering of verse 3, the people bring each main kind of offering in chapters 1-4: burnt offering (1:3), grain offering (2:1), peace offering (3:1) and sin offering (4:3). The grain offering is mixed with oil as 2:4-5 describe.

decisions.choice: today Yahweh will appear to you: a promise of something certain
decisions.reason: The verb form states the event as already settled: Yahweh will surely show himself to the people this very day. Verse 6 says what will appear, "the glory of Yahweh", and verse 23 tells how the promise was kept.

decisions.choice: Do this, because
decisions.reason: Readable turns "for" into a short clause so that the reason stands on its own.

records.source: וַיִּקְח֗וּ אֵ֚ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֣ה מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֶל־פְּנֵ֖י אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד וַֽיִּקְרְבוּ֙ כָּל־הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה וַיַּֽעַמְד֖וּ לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And they took what commanded Moses to [the] face of [the] tent of meeting, and drew near all the congregation and stood before Yahweh.
pieces: So they brought everything Moses had commanded to the area in front of the tent of meeting, and the whole congregation approached and stood there before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.5: And they took what Moses had commanded to the front of the tent of meeting, and all the congregation drew near and stood before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.5: So the people brought everything Moses had commanded to the front of the meeting tent. The whole community came close and stood in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the front of the tent of meeting: the courtyard where the altar stood
decisions.reason: As at the ordination (8:3-4), the people gather in the open space before the tent, where the altar of burnt offering stood (Exodus 40:6, 29). See the note on the tent of meeting at 1:1.

decisions.choice: stood before Yahweh: the people present themselves to God
decisions.reason: To stand before Yahweh is to stand in his presence, at his tent, ready to serve or to receive his word (Deuteronomy 4:10; 10:8). The whole congregation waits for the appearing promised in verse 4.

decisions.choice: community
decisions.reason: Readable says "community" for "congregation", as in 8:3.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֔ה זֶ֧ה הַדָּבָ֛ר אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה תַּעֲשׂ֑וּ וְיֵרָ֥א אֲלֵיכֶ֖ם כְּב֥וֹד יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And said Moses, this [is] the thing which commanded Yahweh, you will do, and will appear to you [the] glory of Yahweh.
pieces: Moses said, "Do this, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded, and the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will appear to you."

L.6: And Moses said, "This [is] the thing that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded [that] you do, and the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will appear to you."

R.6: Moses said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has told you to do this. Do it, and the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will appear to you."

decisions.choice: the glory of Yahweh will appear: God's presence will be seen by the people
decisions.reason: The glory of Yahweh is his presence made visible, a brightness like fire within the cloud. Israel saw it in the wilderness (Exodus 16:7, 10) and on Mount Sinai, "like a consuming fire" on the mountaintop (Exodus 24:16-17). When the tabernacle was finished, the cloud covered it and the glory filled it, so that Moses could not enter (Exodus 40:34-35). God had promised that he would meet Israel at the tent and that it would be made holy by his glory (Exodus 29:42-46). Now that the priests are ordained and the offerings are ready, the glory is to appear to the whole people. Verse 23 tells that it did, and verse 24 that fire came out from it.

decisions.choice: you will do, and it will appear: obedience first, then the appearing
decisions.reason: The two verbs are joined by "and". The glory will appear when the people do what Yahweh has commanded; the second clause gives the result or purpose of the first.

decisions.choice: Do this, as the LORD has commanded (Balanced); Do it (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn "this is the thing ... you will do" into a command, which is its force. Literal keeps the Hebrew shape.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֗ן קְרַ֤ב אֶל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ וַעֲשֵׂ֞ה אֶת־חַטָּֽאתְךָ֙ וְאֶת־עֹ֣לָתֶ֔ךָ וְכַפֵּ֥ר בַּֽעַדְךָ֖ וּבְעַ֣ד הָעָ֑ם וַעֲשֵׂ֞ה אֶת־קָרְבַּ֤ן הָעָם֙ וְכַפֵּ֣ר בַּֽעֲדָ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And said Moses to Aaron, draw near to the altar and do your sin offering and your burnt offering, and make atonement for yourself and for the people, and do [the] offering of the people and make atonement for them, as commanded Yahweh.
pieces: Then Moses told Aaron, "Approach the altar. Offer your sin offering and your burnt offering, and so make atonement for yourself and for the people. Then present the people's offering and make atonement for them, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded."

L.7: And Moses said to Aaron, "Draw near to the altar and offer your sin offering and your burnt offering, and make atonement for yourself and for the people; and offer the offering of the people and make atonement for them, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded."

R.7: Then Moses told Aaron, "Go to the altar. Offer your sin offering and your burnt offering. In this way make atonement for yourself and for the people. Then offer the people's offering and make atonement for them. Do it just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded."

decisions.choice: offer: literally "do" or "make"
decisions.reason: The common verb "do" is used for preparing and presenting an offering (4:20; 14:19). Here it covers the whole work of the priest at the altar.

decisions.choice: make atonement for yourself and for the people: the priest's offering affects the people too
decisions.reason: Aaron's own offerings atone for him, and through him for the people, because a priest's sin brings guilt on the people (4:3). The people's own offering then atones for them. For atonement see 1:4. Hebrews 7:27 recalls that a high priest had to offer first for his own sins and then for the people's.

decisions.choice: and for the people: as the Hebrew reads
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "for yourself and for the people". The Septuagint reads "for yourself and for your house", as in 16:6. The Hebrew reading is kept.

records.source: וַיִּקְרַ֥ב אַהֲרֹ֖ן אֶל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ וַיִּשְׁחַ֛ט אֶת־עֵ֥גֶל הַחַטָּ֖את אֲשֶׁר־לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And drew near Aaron to the altar and slaughtered [the] calf of the sin offering which [was] for him.
pieces: So Aaron went to the altar and slaughtered the calf for his own sin offering.

L.8: And Aaron drew near to the altar and slaughtered the calf of the sin offering that [was] for himself.

R.8: So Aaron went to the altar. He killed the calf for the sin offering for himself.

decisions.choice: slaughtered: the priest kills his own offering
decisions.reason: Normally the one who brings the animal slaughters it (1:5; 4:4). Here Aaron is both the one who brings it and the priest, so he does it himself. For the calf see verse 2.

decisions.choice: killed
decisions.reason: Readable says "killed" for "slaughtered", as in chapter 8.

records.source: וַ֠יַּקְרִבוּ בְּנֵ֨י אַהֲרֹ֣ן אֶת־הַדָּם֮ אֵלָיו֒ וַיִּטְבֹּ֤ל אֶצְבָּעוֹ֙ בַּדָּ֔ם וַיִּתֵּ֖ן עַל־קַרְנ֣וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ וְאֶת־הַדָּ֣ם יָצַ֔ק אֶל־יְס֖וֹד הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃
records.gloss: And brought near [the] sons of Aaron the blood to him, and he dipped his finger in the blood and put [it] on [the] horns of the altar, and the blood he poured out at [the] base of the altar.
pieces: Aaron's sons handed him the blood. He dipped his finger in it and put some on the horns of the altar, and he poured out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.

L.9: And the sons of Aaron brought the blood near to him, and he dipped his finger in the blood and put [it] on the horns of the altar, and the blood he poured out at the base of the altar.

R.9: Aaron's sons brought him the blood. He dipped his finger in it and put some on the horns at the corners of the altar. He poured out the rest of the blood at the bottom of the altar.

decisions.choice: the horns of the altar and its base: the blood rite of the sin offering
decisions.reason: Blood is put on the horns of the altar of burnt offering and the rest poured out at its base, as at the ordination (8:15). In the law for the anointed priest's sin offering the blood is also taken into the tent and sprinkled before the curtain (4:5-7); this chapter does not mention that. For the horns and the base see 4:7.

decisions.choice: the sons of Aaron: Aaron's assistants at the altar
decisions.reason: Aaron's sons serve beside their father, bringing him the blood (verses 12, 18). Aaron, the high priest, does the work at the altar himself on this first day.

decisions.choice: the rest of the blood
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the blood"; Balanced and Readable say "the rest", since some had already been put on the horns.

records.source: וְאֶת־הַחֵ֨לֶב וְאֶת־הַכְּלָיֹ֜ת וְאֶת־הַיֹּתֶ֤רֶת מִן־הַכָּבֵד֙ מִן־הַ֣חַטָּ֔את הִקְטִ֖יר הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חָה כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־מֹשֶֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And the fat and the kidneys and the appendage from the liver from the sin offering he made smoke on the altar, as commanded Yahweh Moses.
pieces: Then on the altar he burned the fat, the kidneys and the long lobe of the liver from the sin offering, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

L.10: And the fat and the kidneys and the appendage of the liver from the sin offering he turned into smoke on the altar, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

R.10: Then he burned the fat, the kidneys and the best part of the liver from the sin offering on the altar. He did just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded Moses.

decisions.choice: the fat, the kidneys, the lobe of the liver: Yahweh's portion of the sin offering
decisions.reason: These are the parts of the sin offering burned on the altar (4:8-10). See the notes at 3:3 and 3:4, and on "turn into smoke" at 1:9.

decisions.choice: as Yahweh had commanded Moses: the first sacrifices follow God's word
decisions.reason: The formula of chapter 8 (8:4) continues: Aaron now does what Yahweh commanded, as Moses had done before him.

records.source: וְאֶת־הַבָּשָׂ֖ר וְאֶת־הָע֑וֹר שָׂרַ֣ף בָּאֵ֔שׁ מִח֖וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And the flesh and the hide he burned with fire outside the camp.
pieces: He burned the meat and the hide in a fire outside the camp.

L.11: And the flesh and the hide he burned with fire outside the camp.

R.11: He burned its meat and its skin outside the camp.

decisions.choice: burned outside the camp: the priest's sin offering is not eaten
decisions.reason: As at the ordination (8:17) and in the law of 4:11-12, the rest of a sin offering made for the priest is burned outside the camp and not eaten. The verb is the ordinary word for burning, not the word for turning an offering into smoke on the altar (verse 10). Compare 10:16-18, where the people's sin offering ought to have been eaten.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁחַ֖ט אֶת־הָעֹלָ֑ה וַ֠יַּמְצִאוּ בְּנֵ֨י אַהֲרֹ֤ן אֵלָיו֙ אֶת־הַדָּ֔ם וַיִּזְרְקֵ֥הוּ עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ סָבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: And he slaughtered the burnt offering, and handed [the] sons of Aaron to him the blood, and he threw it on the altar all around.
pieces: Then Aaron slaughtered the burnt offering. When his sons passed the blood to him, he splashed it on every side of the altar.

L.12: And he slaughtered the burnt offering, and the sons of Aaron handed the blood to him, and he threw it against the altar all around.

R.12: Then Aaron killed the ram for the burnt offering. His sons gave him the blood, and he splashed it on all sides of the altar.

decisions.choice: handed: brought the blood within his reach
decisions.reason: The verb means to cause to find, that is, to hand or pass something to someone. It is used again in verses 13 and 18.

decisions.choice: threw it against the altar all around
decisions.reason: The blood of the burnt offering is thrown from a bowl against the sides of the altar, as in 1:5 and 8:19, not put on the horns with a finger as in verse 9.

decisions.choice: Aaron (Balanced, Readable); the ram (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Aaron as the subject. Readable also says "the ram", since Aaron's burnt offering is the ram of verse 2.

records.source: וְאֶת־הָעֹלָ֗ה הִמְצִ֧יאוּ אֵלָ֛יו לִנְתָחֶ֖יהָ וְאֶת־הָרֹ֑אשׁ וַיַּקְטֵ֖ר עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃
records.gloss: And the burnt offering they handed to him by its pieces, and the head, and he made smoke on the altar.
pieces: His sons passed him the pieces of the burnt offering one by one, and the head as well, and he burned it all on the altar.

L.13: And the burnt offering they handed to him by its pieces, and the head, and he turned [them] into smoke on the altar.

R.13: His sons gave him the burnt offering one piece at a time, with the head. He burned them on the altar.

decisions.choice: by its pieces, and the head: the animal cut up as the law of the burnt offering says
decisions.reason: The burnt offering is cut into its pieces and laid on the altar with the head (1:6, 8, 12). For "turn into smoke" see 1:9.

decisions.choice: His sons
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "they"; Balanced and Readable name Aaron's sons, who handed him the blood in verse 12.

records.source: וַיִּרְחַ֥ץ אֶת־הַקֶּ֖רֶב וְאֶת־הַכְּרָעָ֑יִם וַיַּקְטֵ֥ר עַל־הָעֹלָ֖ה הַמִּזְבֵּֽחָה׃
records.gloss: And he washed the entrails and the legs and made smoke on the burnt offering on the altar.
pieces: The internal organs and the legs he washed, then burned them on the altar on top of the rest of the burnt offering.

L.14: And he washed the entrails and the legs and turned [them] into smoke on the burnt offering on the altar.

R.14: He washed the insides and the legs. Then he burned them on the altar on top of the rest of the burnt offering.

decisions.choice: washed the entrails and the legs: as the law of the burnt offering commands
decisions.reason: See 1:9. The washed parts are laid on the pieces already burning, so that the whole animal goes up in smoke.

decisions.choice: on top of the rest of the burnt offering
decisions.reason: "On the burnt offering" means on the pieces of verse 13 already on the altar; Balanced and Readable say "the rest".

records.source: וַיַּקְרֵ֕ב אֵ֖ת קָרְבַּ֣ן הָעָ֑ם וַיִּקַּ֞ח אֶת־שְׂעִ֤יר הַֽחַטָּאת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָעָ֔ם וַיִּשְׁחָטֵ֥הוּ וַֽיְחַטְּאֵ֖הוּ כָּרִאשֽׁוֹן׃
records.gloss: And he brought near the offering of the people, and took [the] goat of the sin offering which [was] for the people, and slaughtered it and made it a sin offering like the first.
pieces: After that Aaron brought the people's offering forward. He took the goat for their sin offering, slaughtered it, and offered it as a sin offering in the same way as the first.

L.15: And he brought near the offering of the people, and he took the goat of the sin offering that [was] for the people, and slaughtered it and offered it for sin like the first.

R.15: Next Aaron brought the people's offering. He took the goat for the people's sin offering and killed it. He offered it as a sin offering, the same way he had offered the first one.

decisions.choice: offered it for sin: made it a sin offering, to purify
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the same root as "sin offering". It means to offer something as a sin offering and so to cleanse from sin (8:15). See the note on the sin offering at 4:3.

decisions.choice: like the first: in the same way as Aaron's own sin offering
decisions.reason: "The first" is the calf of verses 8-11. The people's goat is offered with the same blood rite. Whether its meat was also burned is not said here; 10:16-18 shows that it should have been eaten by the priests.

decisions.choice: Aaron
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Aaron as the subject.

records.source: וַיַּקְרֵ֖ב אֶת־הָעֹלָ֑ה וַֽיַּעֲשֶׂ֖הָ כַּמִּשְׁפָּֽט׃
records.gloss: And he brought near the burnt offering and did it according to the ordinance.
pieces: He also brought forward the burnt offering and offered it as the rule required.

L.16: And he brought near the burnt offering and offered it according to the ordinance.

R.16: He brought the burnt offering too. He offered it, following the rules for it.

decisions.choice: according to the ordinance: in the way the law sets out
decisions.reason: The word usually means a judgment or ruling; here it is the proper procedure for a burnt offering given in 1:3-13. The people's burnt offering is the calf and the lamb of verse 3.

records.source: וַיַּקְרֵב֮ אֶת־הַמִּנְחָה֒ וַיְמַלֵּ֤א כַפּוֹ֙ מִמֶּ֔נָּה וַיַּקְטֵ֖ר עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ מִלְּבַ֖ד עֹלַ֥ת הַבֹּֽקֶר׃
records.gloss: And he brought near the grain offering and filled his palm from it and made smoke on the altar, besides [the] burnt offering of the morning.
pieces: Then he presented the grain offering. He filled his hand with some of it and burned that on the altar, in addition to the morning burnt offering.

L.17: And he brought near the grain offering and filled his palm from it and turned [it] into smoke on the altar, besides the burnt offering of the morning.

R.17: Then he brought the grain offering. He took a handful of it and burned it on the altar. This was besides the burnt offering made every morning.

decisions.choice: filled his palm: took a handful as the memorial portion
decisions.reason: As 2:2 commands, the priest takes a handful of the grain offering and burns it on the altar. The rest belongs to the priests (2:3; 10:12).

decisions.choice: besides the burnt offering of the morning: the regular daily offering
decisions.reason: A lamb was offered as a burnt offering every morning and every evening, with a grain offering (Exodus 29:38-42; Numbers 28:3-8). The offerings of this day were added to it, not offered in its place.

decisions.choice: made every morning
decisions.reason: Readable says that the morning burnt offering was a daily one, as Exodus 29:38-39 commands.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁחַ֤ט אֶת־הַשּׁוֹר֙ וְאֶת־הָאַ֔יִל זֶ֥בַח הַשְּׁלָמִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָעָ֑ם וַ֠יַּמְצִאוּ בְּנֵ֨י אַהֲרֹ֤ן אֶת־הַדָּם֙ אֵלָ֔יו וַיִּזְרְקֵ֥הוּ עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ סָבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: And he slaughtered the ox and the ram, [the] sacrifice of the peace offerings which [was] for the people, and handed [the] sons of Aaron the blood to him, and he threw it on the altar all around.
pieces: Next he slaughtered the ox and the ram, the peace offering for the people. When Aaron's sons passed him the blood, he splashed it on every side of the altar.

L.18: And he slaughtered the ox and the ram, the sacrifice of peace offerings that [was] for the people, and the sons of Aaron handed the blood to him, and he threw it against the altar all around.

R.18: Next he killed the ox and the ram as the peace offering for the people. Aaron's sons gave him the blood, and he splashed it on all sides of the altar.

decisions.choice: the sacrifice of peace offerings for the people: the offering shared in a meal
decisions.reason: The peace offering is the one whose meat is eaten by those who bring it, after the fat is burned and the priest's share is given (3:1; 7:11-15, 30-34). For the blood see verse 12 and 1:5.

records.source: וְאֶת־הַחֲלָבִ֖ים מִן־הַשּׁ֑וֹר וּמִן־הָאַ֔יִל הָֽאַלְיָ֤ה וְהַֽמְכַסֶּה֙ וְהַכְּלָיֹ֔ת וְיֹתֶ֖רֶת הַכָּבֵֽד׃
records.gloss: And the fats from the ox and from the ram, the fat tail and the covering and the kidneys and [the] appendage of the liver,
pieces: The fat portions from the ox and the ram, the fat tail, the fat that covers the internal organs, the kidneys and the long lobe of the liver,

L.19: And the fat [portions] from the ox and from the ram, the fat tail and the covering, and the kidneys and the appendage of the liver,

R.19: There were also the fat parts of the ox and the ram: the fat tail, the fat that covers the insides, the kidneys and the best part of the liver.

decisions.choice: the fat tail, the covering, the kidneys, the lobe: the fat parts of the peace offering
decisions.reason: These are the parts burned on the altar in 3:3-4 and 3:9-10. The fat tail belongs to the ram, a broad-tailed sheep (3:9); "the covering" is the fat that covers the entrails (3:3). See the notes at 3:3 and 3:4.

decisions.choice: the fat that covers the internal organs (Balanced); the fat that covers the insides (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "the covering"; Balanced and Readable say what it covers, as 3:3 does.

decisions.choice: There were also the fat parts
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sentence runs on into verse 20. Readable makes this verse a sentence of its own.

records.source: וַיָּשִׂ֥ימוּ אֶת־הַחֲלָבִ֖ים עַל־הֶחָז֑וֹת וַיַּקְטֵ֥ר הַחֲלָבִ֖ים הַמִּזְבֵּֽחָה׃
records.gloss: and they put the fats on the breasts, and he made smoke the fats on the altar.
pieces: these fat portions they laid on top of the breasts. Then Aaron burned the fat on the altar.

L.20: and they put the fat [portions] on the breasts, and he turned the fat [portions] into smoke on the altar.

R.20: Aaron's sons put these fat parts on top of the breasts. Then Aaron burned the fat on the altar.

decisions.choice: they put ... he turned into smoke: the sons lay out the fat, Aaron burns it
decisions.reason: "They" are most likely Aaron's sons, who have been helping him (verse 18); "he" is Aaron. The fat is carried to the altar on the breasts, as 7:30 describes.

decisions.choice: Aaron (Balanced, Readable); Aaron's sons (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced names Aaron; Readable names both the sons and Aaron, following the decision above.

records.source: וְאֵ֣ת הֶחָז֗וֹת וְאֵת֙ שׁ֣וֹק הַיָּמִ֔ין הֵנִ֧יף אַהֲרֹ֛ן תְּנוּפָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר צִוָּ֥ה מֹשֶֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And the breasts and [the] thigh of the right Aaron waved [as a] wave offering before Yahweh, as commanded Moses.
pieces: As for the breasts and the right thigh, Aaron waved them before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a wave offering, following Moses' command.

L.21: And the breasts and the right thigh Aaron waved [as] a wave offering before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, just as Moses had commanded.

R.21: Aaron waved the breasts and the right thigh before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a wave offering. He did what Moses had commanded.

decisions.choice: the breasts and the right thigh: the priests' share of the peace offering
decisions.reason: The breast is waved before Yahweh and the right thigh given to the priest (7:30-34). Each animal gave a breast; "the right thigh" is singular, perhaps meaning the right thigh of each. For the wave offering see 7:30.

decisions.choice: as Moses had commanded: as the Hebrew reads
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text reads "as Moses had commanded". The Samaritan Pentateuch and the Septuagint read "as Yahweh had commanded Moses", the formula of verse 10. The Hebrew reading is kept.

records.source: וַיִּשָּׂ֨א אַהֲרֹ֧ן אֶת־יָדָ֛יו אֶל־הָעָ֖ם וַֽיְבָרְכֵ֑ם וַיֵּ֗רֶד מֵעֲשֹׂ֧ת הַֽחַטָּ֛את וְהָעֹלָ֖ה וְהַשְּׁלָמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And lifted up Aaron his hands to the people and blessed them, and came down from doing the sin offering and the burnt offering and the peace offerings.
pieces: Aaron then held out his hands toward the people and blessed them. And when he had finished presenting the sin offering, the burnt offering and the peace offering, he came down from the altar.

L.22: And Aaron lifted up his hands toward the people and blessed them, and he came down from offering the sin offering and the burnt offering and the peace offerings.

R.22: Then Aaron raised his hands toward the people and blessed them. He had finished offering the sin offering, the burnt offering and the peace offering. So he came down from the altar.

decisions.choice: lifted his hands and blessed them: the priest pronounces God's blessing on the people
decisions.reason: Raising the hands toward the people goes with speaking a blessing over them. To bless the people in Yahweh's name was one of the priests' main tasks (Deuteronomy 10:8; 21:5; 1 Chronicles 23:13). The words Aaron used are not given here. Numbers 6:22-27 gives the blessing Aaron and his sons were later told to speak, "Yahweh bless you and keep you", by which they were to put Yahweh's name on Israel; Aaron may have spoken it or words like it. This first blessing comes at the end of the first offerings, when atonement has been made for priest and people, and before the glory appears (verse 23).

decisions.choice: his hands: the reading of the Masoretic margin
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text can be read "his hand"; the Masoretes' marginal reading, followed here, is "his hands". The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: he came down from offering: he came down from the altar after the offerings
decisions.reason: The altar stood higher than the ground, reached by a ramp rather than steps (Exodus 20:26). The clause may mean that Aaron blessed the people from the altar and then came down, or it may sum up that he came down once the offerings were done.

decisions.choice: from the altar
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "came down from doing" the offerings. Balanced and Readable say where he came down from, following the decision above.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֨א מֹשֶׁ֤ה וְאַהֲרֹן֙ אֶל־אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד וַיֵּ֣צְא֔וּ וַֽיְבָרֲכ֖וּ אֶת־הָעָ֑ם וַיֵּרָ֥א כְבוֹד־יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־כָּל־הָעָֽם׃
records.gloss: And went Moses and Aaron into [the] tent of meeting, and they came out and blessed the people, and appeared [the] glory of Yahweh to all the people.
pieces: Moses and Aaron entered the tent of meeting, and on coming out again they blessed the people. Then the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to all the people.

L.23: And Moses and Aaron went into the tent of meeting, and they came out and blessed the people, and the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to all the people.

R.23: Moses and Aaron went into the meeting tent. When they came back out, they blessed the people. Then the glory of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} appeared to all the people.

decisions.choice: the glory of Yahweh appeared to all the people: the promise of verses 4 and 6 is kept
decisions.reason: What Moses promised now happens: Yahweh's presence is seen by the whole people, not by Moses alone. The glory had filled the tent when it was set up (Exodus 40:34-35); now it appears to all Israel as the priests' service begins. The glory appears again at the tent in Numbers 14:10 and 16:19. See the note at verse 6.

decisions.choice: went into the tent and came out: Moses brings Aaron into the holy place
decisions.reason: The text does not say what they did inside. Aaron, now ordained, enters the tent for the first time with Moses, where the priest would tend the lamps, the bread and the incense (Exodus 30:7-8; 40:22-27). When they come out, both bless the people.

records.source: וַתֵּ֤צֵא אֵשׁ֙ מִלִּפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַתֹּ֨אכַל֙ עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ אֶת־הָעֹלָ֖ה וְאֶת־הַחֲלָבִ֑ים וַיַּ֤רְא כָּל־הָעָם֙ וַיָּרֹ֔נּוּ וַֽיִּפְּל֖וּ עַל־פְּנֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And went out fire from before Yahweh and consumed on the altar the burnt offering and the fats; and saw all the people and shouted and fell on their faces.
pieces: Fire went out from before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and devoured the burnt offering and the fat portions lying on the altar. When all the people saw it, they cried out with joy and bowed down with their faces to the ground.

L.24: And fire went out from before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and consumed on the altar the burnt offering and the fat [portions]; and all the people saw [it], and they shouted and fell on their faces.

R.24: Then fire came out from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and burned up the burnt offering and the fat on the altar. All the people saw it. They shouted for joy and bowed down with their faces to the ground.

decisions.choice: fire went out from before Yahweh and consumed: God's own fire accepts the offerings
decisions.reason: The fire comes "from before Yahweh", from his presence at the tent, where the glory had just appeared (verse 23). The offerings were already burning (verses 10-20); now fire from Yahweh consumes them all at once, a sign seen by everyone that he accepts the priests and the people's offerings. Fire from Yahweh marks his acceptance of an offering elsewhere too: for Gideon (Judges 6:21), for David (1 Chronicles 21:26), for Elijah on Mount Carmel (1 Kings 18:38), and at the dedication of Solomon's temple (2 Chronicles 7:1). The fire on the altar was never to go out (6:5-6). In 10:2 the same words tell how fire from before Yahweh consumed Nadab and Abihu.

decisions.choice: shouted: a ringing cry of joy and praise
decisions.reason: The verb means to cry out aloud, and is used mostly of shouting for joy and singing praise (Psalm 33:1; Isaiah 12:6). Here the people's cry greets God's coming with joy, and at the same time they fall down in awe. At the temple's dedication the people, seeing the fire and the glory, likewise bowed to the ground and praised Yahweh (2 Chronicles 7:3).

decisions.choice: fell on their faces: bowed to the ground in worship
decisions.reason: To fall on one's face is to throw oneself to the ground before God in awe and worship (Genesis 17:3; Numbers 16:22; 1 Kings 18:39).

decisions.choice: devoured (Balanced); burned up (Readable)
decisions.reason: The words are the same as in 10:2, and so is the wording: Literal "consumed", Balanced "devoured", Readable "burned up".

decisions.choice: cried out with joy (Balanced); shouted for joy (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that the shout was joyful, following the decision above. Literal keeps "shouted".

decisions.choice: bowed down with their faces to the ground
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what falling on the face means. Literal keeps the idiom.
